author: blu
body: Do not lower it on the argument that some particular app manages with less. The floor is not sized for the median unit, it is sized for the worst DENSITY, and the two units that set it are both small.

author: blu
body: The asymmetry that fixes the guard's strictness: a false positive costs one wasted parse, a false negative lets a quotation through ungated. So the guard must be the loosest thing that cannot miss one.

author: blu
body: A WORK line offers a signed work; an OFFER line offers one with no signature at all. The transport must be able to say which it means: an unsigned work smuggled in as a WORK line with an empty signature would be filed as signed and refused as forged, which answers a different question from the one asked.

author: blu
body: The declared digest on a WORK line is only a claim. It is what the work is filed under, so that a quotation can find it at all; whether the content actually hashes to it is the gate's second guard, not ours.

author: blu
body: An absent trust floor is refused rather than defaulted: a weak default chosen by omission is not a choice. The parser stamps an absent floor as a NEGATIVE sentinel, which is what distinguishes it from a declared floor of zero -- and zero stays legal, admitting only keys the author pinned, at any score.

author: blu
body: The emit brackets carry their own labels because the frontend does not produce as many marks as phase-labels names. Appending them to fe.heap-marks and letting the shared label table number them put h-pre-emit and h-post-emit on the "h8-check" and "h9-lower" slots, so every one of those lines this project has logged reported the emit bracket rather than the phase.
